best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2: keep the gbdt family that already beat the baseline on the ranking axis, but cut its capacity hard so the fit stops memorising the 5,026 training rows. Fit hist_gbdt with max_iter 300, learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 8, min_samples_leaf 60, l2_regularization 10.0, max_features 0.6, early_stopping off (so all 5,026 rows are used and the comparison with iteration 1 is clean), class_weight='balanced', and preprocessing untouched at impute:none / scale:false / no missingness columns. Success is read on the ranking axis first: balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut above 0.7984 and roc_auc above 0.8691 with train_val_gap far below 0.2949 would say regularisation buys ranking; if the gap collapses but the ceiling does not move, the ranking is family/feature-limited and attempt 3 should swap family (xgboost with its own regularisation, or an aggressively-leafed extra_trees) rather than retune inside this one.

critic.evidence: Iteration 1 (hist_gbdt, 400 iters, lr 0.06, 31 leaves, early_stopping off, impute none, class_weight='balanced') scored balanced_accuracy 0.7049 (95% CI 0.6765~0.7358) against the 0.884 bar — short by 0.1791. train_balanced_accuracy 0.9997 vs val 0.7049 gives train_val_gap 0.2949: the model has memorised the 5,026 training rows, which is the dominant, unambiguous signal here. Ranking did improve over the baseline (roc_auc 0.8691 vs 0.8505, pr_auc 0.5878 vs 0.5507, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7984 vs the baseline ceiling 0.7712), so the family swap paid on the ranking axis, but only +0.0272 of best-cut ceiling — far short of the +0.2257 KS the bar demands. On the operating-point axis, recall 0.4855 sits below specificity 0.9243, so the cut is still on the specificity side despite class_weight='balanced', and cut_headroom 0.0935 is only 52% of the 0.1791 still needed. That means at most half the remaining distance is buyable with the cut and the rest is ranking — but the 0.2949 gap says the current ranking is capacity-limited by memorisation, not by family, so the cheapest untried ranking lever is regularising this same fit rather than a fourth family off the same list.
critic.direction: Keep hist_gbdt and attack the 0.2949 train_val_gap with real regularisation — cut capacity hard (fewer, shallower trees, much larger leaves, stronger L2) while leaving preprocessing at impute:none and class_weight='balanced' untouched, so the next row is attributable to the capacity change alone and we learn whether a less-memorised fit lifts balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut above 0.7984.

concrete_changes.preprocessing: unchanged (impute: none, scale: false, missing_indicator: false, missing_count: false)

critic.evidence: Iteration 2 (hist_gbdt, 8 leaves, min_samples_leaf 60, l2 10.0, max_features 0.6, class_weight='balanced', no dropped_hyperparams) scored balanced_accuracy 0.7865 (95% CI 0.7602~0.8114) against the 0.884 bar — short by 0.0975. The overfitting prescription paid and is now spent: train_val_gap fell 0.2949 -> 0.0820, train_balanced_accuracy 0.9997 -> 0.8684, and the paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0816 (95% CI +0.0564~+0.1111, P(better) 1.000), so that movement is real and not the slice. But almost all of it was the operating point, not the ranking: balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut moved only 0.7984 -> 0.8053 (+0.0069) and roc_auc 0.8691 -> 0.8741 (+0.0050), both inside the 0.003~0.006 paired resolution quoted for roc_auc, while cut_headroom collapsed 0.0935 -> 0.0188. That is exactly the "gap collapsed, ceiling did not move" branch the plan itself named. The cut is now near-optimal and balanced (recall 0.7536 vs specificity 0.8193, so no meaningful weight move is left): cut_headroom 0.0188 is only 19% of the 0.0975 still needed, and even a perfect cut of this ranking (0.8053) is 0.0787 below the bar. The bar also sits above the baseline ranking ceiling 0.7712 and demands KS 0.768 (best-cut 0.884) versus this fit's KS ~0.6106, so 0.0787 of ceiling has to come from the ranking. Two hist_gbdt points have now spanned only 0.0069 of best-cut ceiling — retuning inside this family cannot cover 0.0787, and no untried family has been measured here at all (써 본 계열: hist_gbdt only), so the honest read is that the ranking is family/feature-limited. Cost is not a constraint: 5.5s train, 8.1s wall against 600s.
critic.direction: Spend iteration 3 on the ranking axis by swapping family for the first time — fit xgboost at moderate capacity with impute:none held exactly as-is (the only pipeline it can share with hist_gbdt, so the row is attributable to the family alone) and class_weight/scale_pos_weight left at the balanced point that already put recall 0.7536 near specificity 0.8193 — because cut_headroom 0.0188 says only 19% of the remaining 0.0975 is buyable at the operating point and the family's own best-cut ceiling has moved just 0.0069 across two tunings.

critic.evidence: Iteration 3 (xgboost, scale_pos_weight 5.07, impute:none, stopped_at_iter 672/700, no dropped_hyperparams) scored balanced_accuracy 0.7256 (95% CI 0.6917~0.7564) against the 0.884 bar — short by 0.1584. The paired Δ vs iteration 2 is -0.0608 (95% CI -0.0883~-0.0367, P(better) 0.000), so this is a resolved regression, but it is a regression of the *cut*, not the ranking: roc_auc 0.8738 vs 0.8741 and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7986 vs 0.8053 are both inside the 0.003~0.006 paired resolution, while cut_headroom blew back out 0.0188 -> 0.0730 because scale_pos_weight 5.07 did not reproduce hist_gbdt's balanced point (recall 0.5399 far below specificity 0.9114). So the family swap answered exactly what it was sent to answer and the answer was no: two families now span only 0.7986~0.8053 (width 0.0067) of best-cut ceiling, and even a perfect cut of the best of them leaves 0.0787 to the bar — 12x that span. In KS terms the bar needs 0.7680 and the best ranking here is 0.6106. That is what is different from the iteration-2 wrong_model_family verdict, which was issued with only one family measured and no size for the swap: the swap has now been measured and bought 0.0000~0.0067 of ceiling, so a third family off the same list is not a plan that reaches 0.884. train_val_gap 0.2436 (train 0.9692 vs val 0.7256) also says xgboost at depth 5 re-memorised what iteration 2's capacity cuts had fixed. Cost is not a constraint (6.8s train, 9.4s wall of 600s). With 2 iterations left, the bar is unreachable by any lever the executor has on these columns; the recoverable ground is the 0.0730 of cut_headroom, which is 46% of the remaining distance.
critic.direction: Go back to the iteration-2 hist_gbdt configuration — the only fit that put recall (0.7536) near specificity (0.8193) and drove cut_headroom to 0.0188 — and add missing_count as the single change, since the two families' best-cut ceilings span only 0.0067 against a 0.0787 shortfall so the remaining ground is information in the columns plus recovering the balanced operating point, not another estimator.
